problem: Earlier vision-language tasks such as VQA and visual dialog answer questions from a fixed view, with no control over what is seen. Earlier embodied language work used 1-2 room game worlds and low-level 'go to X' commands. No task or benchmark required an agent to navigate a realistic multi-room house from egocentric vision in order to answer a natural-language question.
motivation: Truly intelligent agents must perceive, communicate and act, and question answering can demand active perception: the answer often is not in view at spawn. The authors frame EQA as needing active perception, commonsense priors about where objects are, grounding language into actions, and long-horizon credit assignment. They argue the sparse answer reward is too hard for pure RL, so training must use an instrumented simulator (shortest paths, depth, semantics) for imitation learning and reward shaping, while test time uses RGB only.
key_idea: Define Embodied Question Answering on House3D with a programmatically generated, entropy-balanced question dataset (EQA v1), and solve it with an end-to-end agent. The agent uses a hierarchical Adaptive-Computation-Time navigator (an LSTM planner picks the action, an MLP controller decides how many times to repeat it) plus an attention-based answerer. It is trained by shortest-path imitation learning and then fine-tuned with REINFORCE on answer reward plus distance shaping.
insight: Table 1 compares against an LSTM+Question navigator with identical inputs and outputs. The planner/controller split (ACT+Q) gives the smallest final distance to the target, e.g. d_T 0.46 vs 1.13 at T-10, and is the only imitation-trained model with positive d_Δ. Memory also helps: LSTM models beat reactive CNNs on d_T. RL fine-tuning for answering changes behavior rather than improving navigation: ACT+Q-RL gets closest to the target at some point (lowest d_min) and enters the target room most often (highest %r↲). However, it stops far less often (24-32% vs 100%), overshoots and ends farther away (negative d_Δ at T-10/T-30). It still gets the best mean rank at T-30/T-50. Shortest paths are not optimal vantage points for QA (ShortestPath+VQA MR 3.21 is beaten by several agents). The QA gains are small overall: MR ranges only about 2.99-3.56 across all methods.
method: Vision module: a CNN of 4 {5x5 Conv, ReLU, BatchNorm, 2x2 MaxPool} blocks on 224x224 egocentric RGB. It is pretrained on 100k House3D renders as a multi-task encoder with RGB-reconstruction, 191-class semantic segmentation and depth decoder heads (loss = seg + 10·depth + 10·recon, Smooth-L1 for depth/recon).
Language module: separate 2-layer, 128-d LSTM question encoders for navigation and for answering, since each needs different parts of the question.

ACT navigator: an LSTM planner takes (h_{t-1}, image I_t^0, question Q, previous action) and samples an action in {forward, turn-left, turn-right, stop}. A 1-hidden-layer MLP controller, conditioned on (h_t, a_t, current frame), decides whether to repeat a_t, up to 5 times. This decouples direction from 'velocity' and shortens the planner's effective horizon for gradient flow.

Answering module: dot-product attention of the question over the CNN features of the last five frames. The attention-pooled image feature is combined with the question LSTM encoding, and a softmax is taken over 172 answers.

Imitation pretraining: the navigator is teacher-forced on shortest-path actions to the single queried object with cross-entropy for 15 epochs, under a distance curriculum (start 10 steps back from the target, +10 steps each epoch). The answerer is trained separately on shortest-path frames for 50 epochs.

RL fine-tuning: the answerer is frozen and the navigator is fine-tuned with REINFORCE using a running-average baseline. Reward is 5 for stopping and answering correctly, plus shaping of 0.005 × change in distance to target for forward moves, again with a spawn-distance curriculum.

EQA v1 dataset: CLEVR-style functional programs (select/unique/blacklist/relate/query) run on SUNCG annotations. Questions are filtered by answer-distribution normalized entropy ≥0.5 and appearance in ≥4 environments. v1 uses location, color, color_room and preposition questions over 767 houses with environment-disjoint splits.

setting.backbone: Custom 4-block CNN (multi-task pretrained on House3D renders) + 2-layer 128-d LSTMs (question encoders, planner) + MLP controller + attention answerer, all trained from scratch
setting.training_data: EQA v1 train split: 643 House3D/SUNCG environments, 4246 questions, with automatically generated shortest-path expert demonstrations. CNN pretrained on 100k rendered RGB images with depth/semantic labels from the renderer. RL fine-tuning in the same training environments.
setting.action_space: forward (≤0.25 m), turn-left/turn-right (9°), stop; planner action repeated 1-5 times by controller (no backward/strafe)
setting.privileged: none at test time (RGB only; training uses shortest paths, depth and semantic labels). Test episodes spawn the agent 10/30/50 actions back from the target along the shortest path.

numbers.backbone: custom CNN + LSTM planner + MLP controller (ACT), IL + REINFORCE fine-tuned

numbers_note: This is the early (arXiv/workshop) EQA version on House3D EQA v1, not the later MP3D-EQA benchmark. d_T@T-30 for ACT+Q is printed as 1.50. Metrics are per spawn distance (T_-10/30/50), so they are encoded as metric suffixes. %r_enter corresponds to the paper's %r_↲ (ever entered the target room). The ShortestPath+VQA oracle MR is 3.21 in Table 1, but the appendix states 3.26 for shortest paths (and 3.51 for human navigation + machine QA). HumanNav* was evaluated on a subset of test. There is no success-rate metric. Appendix Table 2 gives CNN segmentation/depth/autoencoder results only.
results: On the EQA v1 test set, the imitation-trained ACT+Q navigator ends closest to the target at every spawn distance: d_T 0.46/1.50/2.74 m vs 1.13/2.23/2.89 m for the strongest baseline, LSTM+Q. It is the only model with positive d_Δ (0.16/0.15/0.12); all baselines end farther from the target than where they started. The RL-fine-tuned ACT+Q-RL has the lowest d_min (0.24/0.93/1.94) and highest room-entry rate at T_-10/T_-30 (65%/62%). It gets the best answer mean rank at T_-30/T_-50 (2.99/3.22 vs LSTM+Q 3.39/3.31), but overshoots and stops only 24-32% of the time. Human teleoperators reach the target room in 86% of cases, far above all agents (≤63%).
limitations: Only 4 single-target question types (EQA v1), with spawns just 10-50 actions from the target along the shortest path. This is a heavily scoped version of the task, and differences in answer mean rank between methods are small (~3.0-3.6 over 172 answers).

The RL-fine-tuned agent overshoots: it rarely stops and ends farther from the target than where it started at T_-10/T_-30. The answerer only sees the last five frames and is frozen during RL, and QA is trained on shortest-path views, so it degrades on human-style views.
Synthetic, non-photorealistic SUNCG/House3D scenes; no real-robot or photorealistic evaluation.
